question: Can the first real multi-terminal KiCad copper tree be imported without rerouting, and can a selected subtree containing shared vias be lowered without detaching it from unselected same-net copper?

tree_import.evaluation: The importer canonicalizes same-layer contacts, contracts same-layer copper contacts within each terminal pad, proves that the resulting uniform copper graph is connected and acyclic, and emits deterministic root-to-terminal paths whose physical union covers every edge. Pad-interior contraction removes 17 redundant stored objects and 1.400408 mm of pad-internal copper; this is electrical graph canonicalization rather than byte preservation. Cycles, dangling material, arcs, zones, non-uniform dimensions, and cross-layer ambiguous pad contacts fail closed.

initial_zero_force_control.evaluation: The selected branches shared trunks with ten unselected branches. Rewriting selected coordinates through f32 displaced them by about 1.3 nanometres from the unselected f64 copper, turning a shared physical edge into 1.379801 mm of duplicate material. KiCad still considered the board connected, but the canonical physical-copper metric rejected the length regression. This exposed missing selected/unselected same-net context coupling.

context_anchor_intermediate.evaluation: Context anchors removed the duplicated edge, but unchanged f32 solver coordinates were still written back as lower-precision f64 values. A 0.000000013 mm numerical artifact was incorrectly accepted as improvement.

corrected_zero_force_control.evaluation: Every selected contact with unselected same-net copper is represented as an exact fixed anchor. Fixed via endpoints and unchanged f32 solver outputs preserve their original f64 coordinates. The full lowering path executes while producing a true byte-identical no-op.

nonzero_motion_regression.fixture: the existing six via-free selected branches [0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9] with rung-42 future copper
nonzero_motion_regression.evaluation: The corrected context model recognizes one more physical contact than selected-only normalization and preserves it with fixed anchors. The result is 0.381629 mm shorter than the earlier independently lowered proposal while retaining byte-identical local/exhaustive behavior and both native gates. This supports useful context-aware nonzero motion, but the selected branches themselves contain no vias.

conclusion.advantage: A real 13-terminal, 12-via tree can cross the board-copper/candidate boundary, and an overlapping selected subtree can enter the uniform particle engine without special component types or loss of physical identity.
conclusion.penalty: Root-to-terminal paths intentionally repeat shared logical prefixes, so lowering must deduplicate physical tension edges and maintain shared groups. Pad-interior contraction is not byte preserving, and cross-layer pad-mediated contacts remain unsupported.
conclusion.scope: This proves topology import and zero-motion representation stability. It does not show that moving the shared subtree improves routing quality or that vias can move, appear, or disappear.
conclusion.next: Use a small shared-via selected neighborhood with nonzero tension to characterize whether fixed via and context anchors overconstrain useful motion, retaining every failed proposal and front/back render before attempting discrete via actions.
